name: MLIR-Functional-Reference-30
description: Hand-authored functional-correctness reference set for arith+func, linalg+memref, and StableHLO (n=30, 10 per dialect). Each record specifies a canonical function name, signature, concrete inputs, and the expected output under a dialect-specific execution wrapper.
citation: Anonymous submission to NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks Track.

distribution.name: test.jsonl
distribution.description: One JSON record per line for the MLIR-Functional-Reference-30 dataset. Generated 1-to-1 from the per-record JSON files in the same directory.

rai:dataCollection: Hand-authored by the submitting author. Each functional reference specifies a canonical MLIR function name, signature, concrete inputs, and the expected scalar/array output under the dialect's execution wrapper (mlir-cpu-runner for arith and linalg+memref; iree-run-module for StableHLO).
rai:dataBiases: Author-curated: prompts reflect the submitting author's mental model of the target dialect; the 10-per-dialect sample biases toward elementary numerical operations.
No human-subject data; no PII; no demographic bias dimensions apply.
rai:dataLimitations: Functional correctness is checked via stdout pattern matching and scalar/array equality on a small set of fixed inputs; this is a coarser signal than property-based or random-input testing.
Each task has exactly one reference implementation; alternate valid implementations may diverge on edge cases.
n=30 is a regression-style spot check, not a comprehensive functional benchmark.
rai:useCases: Spot-checking that verify-valid generations on the sibling Spec-30/Spec-150 benchmarks compute the intended function.
Reporting a verify-vs-functional gap on a hand-authored sample.
rai:excludedUseCases: Comprehensive functional benchmark suitable as the sole metric for ranking systems — size and coverage are insufficient.
Training or fine-tuning production code-generation models.
